messages.subject: Function returned is infinite or NA (non-computable)
parts:
Hi all

I started running BioGeoBEARS with my own data, however when I run the analysis I am getting the following crash:

d    e a b x u    j  ysv    ys     y     s     v mx01 mx01j mx01y mx01s mx01v mx01r  mf dp fdp LnL
1 0.01 0.01 0 1 0 0 0.01 2.99 1.993 0.997 0.997 0.997    0     0     0     0     0   0.5 0.1  1   0 NaN
Maximizing -- use negfn and neggr
    
 d    e a b x u    j  ysv    ys     y     s     v mx01 mx01j mx01y mx01s mx01v mx01r  mf dp fdp LnL
1 0.01 0.01 0 1 0 0 0.01 2.99 1.993 0.997 0.997 0.997    0     0     0     0     0   0.5 0.1  1   0 NaN

Error in optimx(par = params, fn = calc_loglike_for_optim, gr = NULL,  : 
  Function returned is infinite or NA (non-computable)


I thougt this error was due to the last version of Optimx, however I installed the older Optimx version from 2012 and I am getting the same error. Any ideas about what may cause this error?

Cheers!

messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Function returned is infinite or NA (non-computable)
parts:
So, this happens when some step (looks like the first step, for you?)
of the ML search produces a NaN for the likelihood. I don't remember
exactly, but I've occasionally experienced things like this sometimes
with e.g. dispersal matrices, but it might also occur on different
operating systems, if they make different assumptions about machine
precision. Also, the optim and optimx functions are supposed to limit
the parameter search within the limits specified for each parameter.

Another possibility is a tree with 0-length branches, negative-length
branches, or polytomies. The default functions check for the problems
I know about but you may have discovered another, or may have skipped
a check somehow.

So, options:

- check that tree has nothing weird like 0-length branches,
negative-length branches, or polytomies

- check that the geography file has no anomalies (all species have
ranges between 1 and max_num_areas)

- replace 0 with e.g. 0.0000001 if you are using a manual dispersal matrix etc.

- play with the lower and upper limits on the parameters you are searching.

Report back if you figure it out! If those fail, send me the files
and I can see if I can replicate the problem.

Cheers!
Nick

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Function returned is infinite or NA (non-computable)
parts: Just an update -- looking at the files, I figured out that this error:

On Tuesday, November 12, 2013 10:20:51 PM UTC-5, Nick Matzke wrote:
>
> d    e a b x u    j  ysv    ys     y     s     v mx01 mx01j mx01y mx01s
> mx01v mx01r  mf dp fdp LnL
> 1 0.01 0.01 0 1 0 0 0.01 2.99 1.993 0.997 0.997 0.997    0     0     0     0
> 0   0.5 0.1  1   0 NaN
> Maximizing -- use negfn and neggr
>
>  d    e a b x u    j  ysv    ys     y     s     v mx01 mx01j mx01y mx01s
> mx01v mx01r  mf dp fdp LnL
> 1 0.01 0.01 0 1 0 0 0.01 2.99 1.993 0.997 0.997 0.997    0     0     0     0
> 0   0.5 0.1  1   0 NaN
>
> Error in optimx(par = params, fn = calc_loglike_for_optim, gr = NULL,  :
>   Function returned is infinite or NA (non-computable)

... resulted from having a species missing from the geography file. This can be checked for with this command:

=============
check_BioGeoBEARS_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object)
=============

Cheers!
Nick
